summary: Kixx was U.S. Gold's budget re-release label, returning established computer games to the shelves at a lower price across the late 1980s and 1990s.
facts: The Mastertronic Collectors Archive records that U.S. Gold created its own budget label Kixx after previously supplying older full-price titles to third-party budget ranges.
The Centre for Computing History preserves Kixx releases across home-computer formats, including Commodore 64 and Commodore Amiga editions.
The preserved Kixx catalogue includes explicit re-releases of earlier games alongside arcade, sports and racing titles.
note: Kixx is shown by CCG as a re-release publisher when a game record credits the label in its re-release field; the original publisher credit remains intact.

summary: The Hit Squad was a prominent budget re-release range associated with Ocean-era home-computer software, returning established titles to market across several computer formats.
facts: The Centre for Computing History preserves a large catalogue of releases published under The Hit Squad name across several home-computer formats.
Its Commodore 64 collection includes titles explicitly described by the museum as budget re-releases, alongside arcade conversions, film licences and sports games.
The museum collection also preserves The Hit Squad releases for the Commodore Amiga, including games associated with Ocean Software and other developers or publishers.
note: The Hit Squad is shown by CCG as a re-release publisher when a game record credits the label in its re-release field; the original publisher credit remains intact.
